records.issue.container_mib: The container size must be greater than zero.
records.issue.tail_negative: The volume capacity ({mounted}) is greater than the container without the VeraCrypt headers ({volume}). Check container_mib and mounted_bytes.
records.issue.tail_unusual: The volume capacity is {tail} B less than the container without the VeraCrypt headers, while NTFS keeps back exactly one cluster, {cluster} B. Check container_mib and mounted_bytes.
records.issue.free_ge_mounted: The free space on the empty volume ({free}) is not less than its capacity ({mounted}).
records.issue.ntfs_range: The NTFS metadata came out at {ntfs} B, outside the plausible range {low}..{high} B. Looks like lost or extra digits.
records.issue.consumed_lt_file: {consumed} B is used on the volume, while the file itself takes {alloc} B. The used space cannot be less than the file: one of the fields empty_free_bytes / left_bytes / file_bytes is wrong.
records.issue.alloc_lt_logical: The data rounded to clusters ({alloc}) is less than its logical size ({logical}). Rounding up cannot make it smaller.
records.issue.alloc_not_aligned: The data rounded to clusters ({alloc}) is not a multiple of the cluster size ({cluster}).
records.issue.file_count: The file count must be at least 1.
records.issue.file_count_gt_bytes: There are more files ({count}) than bytes ({bytes}).
records.error.corrupt: The file {path} is damaged and does not read as JSON: {error}. Backup copy: {backup}
records.error.schema: Schema version {version} is not supported; expected one of: {supported}.
model.safety.ntfs.uncalibrated: the NTFS model is not calibrated: the default value
model.safety.ntfs.extrapolation: the size is outside the measured range: a cautious estimate over all records at once
model.safety.ntfs.exact: the model does not underestimate here: a measurement is close, the chord runs above
model.safety.ntfs.neighbours: the miss on records of a similar size, scaled to this segment
model.safety.ntfs.bend: the bend of the curve between the neighbouring measurements
model.safety.ntfs.factory: ; the segment rests on factory measurements
model.safety.slack.one_file: one file: the constant part of copy slack is measured, the risk is small
model.safety.slack.default: no measurement with a similar file count, and there are {count} files: the default value
model.safety.slack.neighbours: the miss on measurements with a similar file count
charts.ntfs_curve.note: The model draws a straight line between neighbouring measurements, but the dependence is not a straight line: $LogFile changes in steps.

charts.ntfs_curve.uncovered.one: Not covered by measurements: {n} size — {names}; there the line runs through empty space.
charts.ntfs_curve.uncovered.other: Not covered by measurements: {n} sizes — {names}; there the line runs through empty space.

charts.ntfs_curve.title: NTFS metadata by volume size
charts.ntfs_residuals.title: NTFS model miss, leave-one-out check
charts.ntfs_residuals.note: Zero is the model itself. Up is an underestimate, the only dangerous side: the container would have been short by that much. The edge measurements are hidden — without them the model extrapolates, and the miss there is orders of magnitude larger; a click on the legend brings them back.
charts.ntfs_share.title: Share of the volume taken by metadata
charts.ntfs_share.note: How much of the volume goes to something other than data. The neighbouring slope chart is about something else: the rate of growth over a segment, not the level.
charts.ntfs_slopes.title: Slope of the NTFS model segments
charts.ntfs_slopes.note: A flat step is a stretch where metadata grows in proportion to the volume. A jump is a threshold where the size of $LogFile changed.
charts.slack_curve.no_slope: Slope not measured: it needs measurements at two different n.
charts.slack_curve.title: Copy slack by file count
charts.slack_residuals.title: Copy slack model miss, leave-one-out check
charts.slack_residuals.note: Zero is the model itself. Up is an underestimate.
charts.forecast.tip:
{id}
Promised: {predicted} MiB
Would have sufficed: {minimum} MiB
Overestimate: {miss} MiB
Including safety margin: {safety} MiB
charts.forecast.note: Everything above zero is overestimate. A point below zero means the data would not have fitted without the safety margin.

charts.forecast.short.one: Below zero: {n} record — there only the safety margin saved the calculation.
charts.forecast.short.other: Below zero: {n} records — there only the safety margin saved the calculation.

charts.forecast.title: Prediction miss by record
charts.breakdown.title: Container {container} MiB — what it is made of
charts.breakdown.note: Of these, cluster tail: {tail} — the cost of rounding each file up to a cluster.
charts.cluster_tail.title: Used space by cluster size
charts.cluster_tail.note: Files: {files}. The distance between the lines is the cluster tail, the cost of rounding each file up.
collect.self_check.mismatch: The self-check did not match: the dynamic container with quick format gave {fast} B of metadata, the normal one with full format {slow} B, a difference of {difference} B. Dynamic containers measure differently on this machine, and the other sizes cannot be run on them: the numbers would not describe the containers that will actually be created.
collect.error.set_too_big: The file set "{fileset}" takes {alloc} with a {cluster} B cluster, and the volume has {free} free. The measurement was not started.
collect.error.file_count: Files on the volume: {found}; the file set "{fileset}" consists of {expected}. The measurement is unusable.
collect.error.disk_floor: Less than {floor} is left on the disk — writing stopped so as not to break the volume halfway.
fileset.one.title: One 64 MiB file
fileset.fifty.title: 50 files of 10 MiB
fileset.small_500.title: 500 files of 1 KiB
fileset.small_5000.title: 5 000 files of 1 KiB
fileset.small_10000.title: 10 000 files of 1 KiB
fileset.mixed.title: 500 × 1 KiB + 50 × 10 MiB + 1 × 1 GiB
fileset.huge.title: One 4 GiB file
veracrypt.install.title: {directory} (version {version})
veracrypt.missing.binary: Folder {path} has no binary for {lacking}. "{format_name}" and "{mount_name}" are needed; a portable build has the same names with an architecture suffix.
veracrypt.version.unreadable: Could not read the VeraCrypt version. The volume will be unmounted with the old /dismount switch — every version understands it.
veracrypt.version.too_old: VeraCrypt {version} is too old: the /nosizecheck and /quick switches appeared in 1.24. Without the first, a terabyte container refuses to be created unless a terabyte is free. 1.24 or newer is needed.
veracrypt.version.noisy_create: VeraCrypt {version}: before 1.25.4 the /silent switch did not remove the wait window when creating an NTFS container. Collection will run, but the window will pop up for every container.
veracrypt.version.dismount: VeraCrypt {version}: the volume will be unmounted with the /dismount switch — /unmount appeared only in 1.26.20.
veracrypt.run.timeout: {program} did not respond within {timeout} s and was stopped.
veracrypt.create.missing: Container {name} was not created (exit code {code}). Most often the cause is missing rights: NTFS formatting requires an administrator, and in silent mode VeraCrypt says nothing about it.
veracrypt.create.size: Container {name} came out {actual} B instead of {expected} B. A measurement from such a container would land in the wrong row.
veracrypt.mount.timeout: Volume {letter}: did not mount within {timeout} s (exit code {code}). Check that the VeraCrypt driver is installed and running.

veracrypt.unmount.failed.one: Volume {letter}: did not unmount in {n} attempt (last exit code {code}). While it is mounted, the container file cannot be deleted.
veracrypt.unmount.failed.other: Volume {letter}: did not unmount in {n} attempts (last exit code {code}). While it is mounted, the container file cannot be deleted.

veracrypt.letters.none: No free drive letters are left.
paths.argument.unwritable: The folder from {argument} is not writable: {path}
paths.origin.unwritable: the program folder is not writable
app.title: ContainerHelper — VeraCrypt container size
tab.calc.tip:
Pick files and folders — or type a size by hand — and get Container init for VeraCrypt.
You can also see what that number is made of.
tab.records.tip:
Records of real copies: which container, what went into it, how much was left. Copy slack is calibrated on them.
Empty-volume measurements are not here but on the Calibration tab.
tab.model.tip:
What both models rest on and how far they miss on their own measurements: each one is predicted by a model built without it.
Nothing to edit here, this is diagnostics.
tab.calibration.tip:
How well the sizes are covered by empty-volume measurements. Such a measurement needs no data — metadata depends only on the volume size.
Come here when the calculation is marked as extrapolation.
app.data_dir.title: Where to keep the data
app.data_dir.text: The folder next to the program is not writable. Choose a folder for the records and settings — it will be remembered for this copy of the program.
app.chart.breakdown.title: What the container is made of
app.chart.breakdown.empty: The calculation is empty: pick sources or type a size.
app.chart.cluster.title: Used space by cluster size
app.chart.cluster.empty: Calculated from the real file sizes — pick sources.
app.remove_slack.title: Remove measurement
app.remove_slack.text: Remove "{name}"? The numbers will disappear from the file; this cannot be undone.
app.reset_points.title: Revert to factory
app.reset_points.text:
Disable your own empty-volume measurements ({n}) and calculate with the factory ones?
The numbers stay in the file — each one can be enabled again. Copy-slack measurements are not affected.
app.expand_tables.tip: Stretch the tables to all their rows. The tab becomes taller than the window and scrolls. The height of each table can also be dragged separately — by the strip under it.
app.remember_tab.tip:
Open the program on the tab where it was closed.
Off — the program always opens on the {tab} tab.
app.units.tip: What unit the byte columns are shown in. Input, storage and Container init itself are not affected.
app.language.tip: The language of the windows. Switches at once, in every open window; names and notes keep the language they were typed in.
picker.title: Choose files and folders
picker.select_all.tip: Select everything in this folder. Ctrl+A does the same.
picker.select_none.tip: Release the selection without closing the dialog.
picker.invert.tip: Select everything except what is selected now. An easier way to take a whole folder without two or three names.
picker.remember.tip:
Open where it was closed last time. Off — open on "My Computer", with the list of drives.
The folder shown is remembered, not the one selected in it: the next choice usually lies next to the last one.
picker.hidden.tip:
The dialog does not inherit the Explorer setting but keeps its own — it is saved in the data folder next to the other view settings.
Does not affect the calculation: inside a selected folder hidden files are always counted, the walk does not skip them.
picker.hint: A double-click enters a folder, "Select" takes the whole selection. You can draw a frame with the mouse; Ctrl and Shift select one by one and in a run — files and folders can be mixed. A folder inside another selected folder is not counted twice.
calc.source.none: No source selected: drop files and folders here, select them with the button, or type the size by hand.
calc.size.tip:
Data size in bytes; digit-group separators may stay.
Filled in by itself once sources are selected. If corrected by hand, the link to the selected paths is lost, and the file count has to be entered by hand too.
calc.count.tip: How many files. Copy slack depends on it: each file takes an MFT record and a place in the directory index.
calc.pick.tip:
Select files and folders — in one list, any mix. Replaces what is selected now.
A folder counts whole. Paths nested in one another are not counted twice.
calc.add.tip: The same window, but the selection is added to what is already gathered. The dialog shows only one folder at a time, and data comes from different places.
calc.drop.tip: Remove the selected rows. Ctrl+A selects all — that clears the set entirely and lets you go back to manual input.
calc.select.all.tip: Select all sources. Ctrl+A does the same.
calc.select.none.tip: Clear the selection from all rows — "Remove" is disabled after that.
calc.select.invert.tip: Select everything except what is selected now. This is how to remove all but one or two sources you need.
calc.src.tip: What each source brought. Rows go in the order of selection.
calc.src.col.source.tip: What was selected. The full path is in the row's tooltip.
calc.src.col.kind.tip: A folder counts whole, with everything nested in it. A file counts by itself.
calc.src.col.files.tip: How many files are inside. The more of them, the larger the copy slack: each needs an MFT record and a place in the index.
calc.src.col.folders.tip: How many nested folders were scanned. Hardly affects the size, but shows the scan reached the end.
calc.src.col.logical.tip: The sum of the file sizes — the same as Explorer shows.
calc.src.col.alloc.tip: How much the data will take on the volume: each file is rounded up to a cluster. On small files noticeably more than the logical size.
calc.source.sizes: Logical size {logical} B, cluster-rounded {alloc} B (cluster tail {tail} B).
calc.source.file_sizes: File: largest {largest} B, smallest {smallest} B, average {average} B.
calc.source.empty_files: Empty files: {count} — they take no cluster space, but each needs an MFT record.
calc.cluster.tip:
The step in which the filesystem hands out space: a 1-byte file takes a whole cluster, a 4097-byte file with a 4096 cluster takes two.
On one large file the choice changes almost nothing, on 500 small ones it is 2 MiB against 32 MiB.
Every filesystem has clusters, but we measured metadata only on NTFS.
calc.safety.tip: A margin on top of the calculation — in case the models missed slightly.
calc.auto_safety.tip: Compute the safety margin for this size and file count instead of keeping one number for all calculations.
calc.safety.empty: Fitted from the records — the calculation is empty so far.
calc.copy.tip: Copy the MiB number to enter in VeraCrypt.
calc.breakdown.tip:
What Container init is made of. Rows go in the order they add up, so they are not sorted.
Hover over a row to see where the component comes from.
calc.col.component.tip: A component of the container size. Rows go in the order they add up, "Total" is their sum.
calc.col.bytes.tip: The value in bytes. Does not follow the display unit: it is the one to reconcile with what VeraCrypt and Explorer show.
calc.col.unit.tip: The same in the chosen unit. For "B" it shows MiB — two identical columns are of no use.
calc.row.payload.tip: The data itself, but each file rounded up to a cluster — the filesystem hands out space only in clusters.
calc.row.cluster_tail.tip: How much of the row above went to rounding. Grows with the file count and the cluster size.
calc.row.vc_header.tip: 262 144 B — the VeraCrypt headers at the start of the container file and their backups at the end. Everything else goes to the volume.
calc.row.metadata.tip: What the filesystem keeps for itself: $MFT, $LogFile, $Bitmap and the rest, plus one cluster at the end of the volume that NTFS does not show even in the capacity. Depends on the volume size, not on the content. Taken from the measurements on the "Calibration" tab.
calc.row.copy_slack.tip: How much the files take beyond their cluster-rounded size: an MFT record for each and the growth of the directory indexes.
calc.row.safety.tip: A correction for the models' error. In "Auto" mode it is computed for this volume size and this file count.
calc.row.total.tip: Everything above, rounded up to whole MiB. This is the number entered in VeraCrypt.
calc.row.left.tip: How much space should remain on the volume after copying. It can be checked with the "Measure left space" button in the record.
calc.note.extrapolated: The size is outside the measured range, the NTFS metadata is computed by extrapolation. Take a measurement close to this size — an empty container is enough.

calc.note.slack_default.one: Copy slack for {n} file ({size}) is the default value: there are no records with several files yet.
calc.note.slack_default.other: Copy slack for {n} files ({size}) is the default value: there are no records with several files yet.

calc.note.manual_many: The size was typed by hand for several files. Cluster rounding is computed once for the whole sum, not for each file, so in practice it will come out larger. Select a folder — we will compute it exactly.
calc.note.unread:
Part of the data was not read, the calculation is underestimated:
{shown}{more}
records.col.name: Name
records.col.name.tip: What the record is called. Needed only to recognise it in the checks on the Model tab.
records.col.container.tip: The size entered in VeraCrypt when the container was created. Without the VeraCrypt headers it is the volume size, which the NTFS metadata depends on.
records.col.capacity.tip: What the mounted volume reports: the volume size less the one cluster NTFS keeps for itself. The difference reveals a typo in the container size.
records.col.metadata.tip: The volume size (the container without the VeraCrypt headers) minus the empty free space. Computed on the fly, not written to the file.
records.col.deviation.tip: How far the measurement departs from the default model (19 MiB + 0.17 % of the volume). From it, not from the calibrated one: that passes through its own points, and the deviation would always be zero.
records.col.files.tip: How many files were copied. Empty means the measurement was taken on an empty volume.
records.col.left.tip: Free space after copying, VeraCrypt's Left space. Copy slack is calibrated by it.
records.col.miss.tip:
What the calculation promised minus what would have just sufficed. The minimum is derived from the measured left space: the used space on the volume plus the VeraCrypt header, rounded up.
Plus is an overestimate, minus means the data would not have fitted. The column exists for the second case: underestimate is the only dangerous side of the calculation.
Empty means no prediction was recorded: fill in "Promised by calculation" in the record or bring the calculation over with the "Take from Calculation" button.
records.col.model_miss.tip:
The same miss less the safety margin: how far the models themselves were off.
Without it the miss is ambiguous: +5 MiB looks the same when the model is exact with a 5 MiB safety margin and when the model underestimated by 3 and 8 MiB of safety margin hid it. The second is a forerunner of failure.
records.col.status.tip:
"ok": the record is fit for calibration.
"errors": something does not add up, details in the row tooltip.
"flagged": saved anyway and kept out of calibration.
records.path.tip:
Copy records. The empty-volume measurements lie next to it, in Calibration.json: they describe the machine, not the data, and are no good on another machine.
Both files are in the data folder next to the program, which is carried as a whole.
records.path.backup.tip: One backup copy with the .bak extension lies next to the file.
records.choose.tip:
Open another records file or start a new one. An existing file is read, not overwritten.
The measurements come from Calibration.json in the same folder.
records.add.tip: Create a copy record: the container size, the volume measurements and the left space after copying.
records.edit.tip: Open the selected record. A double click on the row does the same.
records.delete.tip: Remove the selected record. It cannot be undone, so you will be asked to confirm.
records.chart.tip:
The promised size against the one that would have just sufficed, with a band for the safety margin included.
The window is modeless: it can be left alongside to watch the picture change after a new measurement.
records.table.tip:
Copy records; the empty-volume measurements live on the Calibration tab.
A click on a header sorts: ascending, descending, unsorted. A double click on a row opens the record.
records.summary.tip:
What the records themselves give the models. Empty-volume measurements are not counted here: their coverage is shown on the Calibration tab.
Only records with a data size and a left space calibrate copy slack, and separating the per-file slack takes records with different file counts.
records.lost.title: Record not found
records.lost.text: "{id}" was deleted while its edit window was open. The changes were not saved.
records.delete.title: Delete record
records.row.short: The promised container would not have held this data.
records.summary.points: Points for the NTFS model: {count} (volumes {low}…{high} B).
records.summary.no_points: Points for the NTFS model: {count} — the model runs on default values.
records.summary.no_slack: Copy-slack measurements: {count} — the per-file slack is not confirmed.
records.forecast.unchecked: The prediction is checked against nothing: no record has "Promised by calculation" filled in.
records.forecast.short: Prediction checked on {checked}: underestimated on {count} — {names}; worst miss {worst} MiB.
records.forecast.held: Prediction checked on {checked}: never underestimated, smallest overestimate {worst} MiB (of which {model} MiB is the miss of the models themselves, the rest is safety margin).
record.title: Measurement record
record.group.derived: Computed automatically, not written to the file
record.id.tip: What the record will be called in the tables. It does not affect the calculation, but a record without a name cannot be saved: it could not be found in the checks.
record.payload.tip: Bring over Container init, the cluster size, the data size, the file count and the cluster-rounded size — exactly those the calculation used.
record.measure.tip: Read the capacity and the free space of the empty mounted volume.
record.left.tip: Take the free space after copying, and check along the way that the volume holds exactly what the container was calculated for.
record.container.tip: Container init is what was entered in VeraCrypt at creation. Not the size of the file on disk: the file is larger than the volume by the header.
record.cluster.tip:
The step in which the filesystem hands out space. A measurement reads it from the volume by itself; by hand it is needed only for a record made after the fact.
A typo here silently spoils copy slack.
record.capacity.tip:
What the mounted volume reports: the container without the VeraCrypt headers and without the one cluster NTFS keeps for itself. This difference reveals a typo in the container size.
Taken with the "Measure volume" button.
record.empty_free.tip: Free space right after formatting, before copying. The volume size (the container without the VeraCrypt headers) minus this number is the NTFS metadata.
record.data.tip:
The size of what was copied, as Explorer shows it.
Empty means the volume was empty; such a record does not calibrate copy slack.
record.files.tip: How many files were copied. The per-file slack is calibrated by this number, but only if there are several records and their file counts differ.
record.alloc.tip: How much the data took with each file rounded up to a cluster. For a single file it may be left empty — it is computed. For a folder it is not, and without this number copy slack comes out overstated.
record.left_space.tip:
Free space after copying, VeraCrypt's Left space. The difference from "Free when empty" is how much the data actually took.
Taken with the "Measure left space" button.
record.predicted.tip:
The Container init the program advised for this data. Filled in by the "Take from Calculation" button.
Stored, not recomputed: both models change with every new measurement, and recomputing after the fact would answer "what would I say today", not "what did I say then".
Empty means there is nothing to check the prediction against.
record.predicted_safety.tip: How much safety margin the promise included. Without this number the miss is ambiguous: +5 MiB looks the same when the model is exact with a 5 MiB safety margin and when the model underestimated by 3 and 8 MiB of safety margin hid it.
record.note.tip: Free text for yourself: what was copied, on which machine, what looked odd. Takes no part in the calculation.
record.minimum.tip:
The smallest container this data would still have fitted into: the used space on the volume plus the VeraCrypt header, rounded up to MiB.
The estimate is slightly high — a smaller container would also have had less metadata — so the miss comes out smaller than the real one. An error on the side of alarm, not of complacency.
record.miss.tip: Promised minus the smallest sufficient. Minus means the data would not have fitted — this case is what the check is for.
record.prompt.empty: Mount the empty formatted container and choose its letter. The volume capacity and its free space are read.
record.prompt.left: Mount the container with the data already copied and choose its letter. The left free space is read.
record.left.no_files: There are no files on volume {drive}. Left space is measured after copying; for an empty volume there is "Measure volume".
record.verdict.service_dirs: NTFS system folders on the volume: {dirs}. They take space but do not count as files.
record.verdict.unchecked: On volume {drive}: {count} files, {alloc} B cluster-rounded. Nothing to reconcile with — fill in the data size and the file count.
record.verdict.alloc_mismatch: {found} B cluster-rounded on the volume, {expected} B expected
record.verdict.mismatch: ⚠ The volume contents do not match the calculation: {details}. Copy slack must not be taken from such a record.

record.verdict.match.one: The contents of volume {drive} match the calculation: {n} file, {alloc} B cluster-rounded.
record.verdict.match.other: The contents of volume {drive} match the calculation: {n} files, {alloc} B cluster-rounded.

record.verdict.unread.one: Part of the volume was not read ({n} path).
record.verdict.unread.other: Part of the volume was not read ({n} paths).

record.payload.none: The Calculation tab has no data: choose a file or folder, or enter a size.
record.no_name: Enter a name for the record.
record.miss.none: —  (needs "Promised by calculation" and the left space after copy)
record.miss.short: {miss} MiB — the data would not have fitted; of this, the models missed by {model} MiB, the rest is safety margin.
record.miss.exact: {miss} MiB — just enough; of this, the models missed by {model} MiB, the rest is safety margin.
record.miss.over: {miss} MiB — overestimate; of this, the models missed by {model} MiB, the rest is safety margin.
model.col.record.tip: Whose measurement this is. The record itself is on the Records or Calibration tab.
model.col.measured.tip: What the real volume showed. This is what we compare against.
model.col.predicted.tip: What the model would give without this measurement. Otherwise it would pass exactly through its own point, and there would be nothing to check.
model.col.deviation.tip: Measured minus predicted. Plus: the model underestimated, and the safety margin must cover the difference. Minus: it allowed too much.
model.col.basis.tip:
"calibration": the prediction rests on other measurements.
"default": there were not enough measurements, the default formula worked.
model.chart.ntfs.tip:
The NTFS curve, the leave-one-out miss and the slope of each segment — in one window, with a shared axis.
The window is modeless: it can stay alongside and show how the picture changes after a new measurement.
model.chart.slack.tip:
Measured copy slack against the file count with the model line, and under them the leave-one-out miss.
The window is modeless: it can stay alongside and show how the picture changes after a new measurement.
model.state.title: Calibration status
model.state.tip: How many measurements both models rest on and what range they cover.
model.state.ntfs.tip:
NTFS metadata as a function of the volume size. Inside the range covered by measurements the calculation uses them, outside it the base growth from the edge.
A point can be added on the Calibration tab.
model.state.slack.tip:
How much the files take beyond their cluster-rounded size: a constant part plus so much per file.
The per-file part shows only on records with different file counts; with one and the same count it stays a guess.

model.state.ntfs.calibrated.one: NTFS: {n} point, volumes {low}…{high} B ({low_gib}…{high_gib} GiB). Inside the range the measurements are used, outside it the base growth of {rate} % from the edge of the measurements.
model.state.ntfs.calibrated.other: NTFS: {n} points, volumes {low}…{high} B ({low_gib}…{high_gib} GiB). Inside the range the measurements are used, outside it the base growth of {rate} % from the edge of the measurements.

model.state.ntfs.default: NTFS: points: {n}, at least two are needed. The default model is in use: {base} MiB + {rate} % of the volume size.

model.state.slack.one_count.one: {n} measurement, at n = {files}; the per-file part remained an assumption
model.state.slack.one_count.other: {n} measurements, all at n = {files}; the per-file part remained an assumption

model.state.slack.none: no measurements, both parts are defaults
model.margin.title: Safety margin
model.margin.tip: The safety margin is only shown here. It is edited on the Calculation tab: it depends on the volume size and the file count, and only that tab knows them.
model.margin.value.tip: How much is added on top of the calculation and where the number comes from — computed automatically or set by hand.
model.margin.hint.tip: This is a reference, not a requirement. The check measures the model without one point, that is, one sparser than the real one, and its miss does not shrink with new measurements. Keeping a safety margin by it at all sizes means paying everywhere for the emptiest spot of the grid.
model.margin.no_records: Nothing to check against: no records.
model.margin.diagnostic: Worst underestimate in the leave-one-out check: {worst}. This is an estimate of the model without one point, not a requirement for the safety margin.
model.margin.auto: {value} — fitted to each calculation on the Calculation tab.
model.margin.manual: {value} — set by hand on the Calculation tab.
model.check.explanation: Each measurement is predicted by a model built without it — otherwise the deviation would always be zero.
model.check.table.tip:
{title}: each measurement against the model built without it.
A click on a header sorts: ascending, descending, unsorted.
model.check.summary.tip: Where the model underestimated the most. An underestimate is dangerous, the safety margin must cover it; an overestimate costs only extra space.
model.check.under.tip: The model underestimated — the safety margin must cover this.
model.check.shortfall: Largest underestimate: {shortfall}. The safety margin must be no less.
model.check.no_shortfall: The model underestimated nowhere; largest overestimate {overestimate}.
chart.detach.tip: Show this chart in a separate window. The zoom and the hidden series move with it.
chart.return.tip: Put the chart back in its place in the shared window. Closing this window does the same.
chart.move.left: Swap with the chart on the left.
chart.move.right: Swap with the chart on the right.
chart.empty: No measurements yet — nothing to draw.
chart.save.title: Save chart
chart.save.name: chart
chart.hint: Drag a frame with the left button to zoom in, the wheel zooms, hold the right button to pan, right double-click or Esc resets. The menu is on a left double-click or the middle button. A click on the legend hides a series, a click on a point shows it in full.
chart.grid.tip: Lay the charts out two in a row. The window gets lower and wider — vertical space is dearer.
chart.column.tip: Put the charts in a column, one under another.
chart.even.tip: A double click divides the height equally
chart.sync.tip:
Keep the same stretch of the X axis as the charts of the same group.
Off: the window keeps its own zoom.
chart.cross.tip:
Show the vertical line under the cursor on the neighbouring charts — at the same X value, each in its own zoom.
This is what the shared axis is for: the hump in the residuals stands right under its step in the slope.
chart.reset.tip: Return all charts of the window to the full view. A right double-click on a chart or Esc does the same.
chart.copy.tip: Put the chart on the clipboard. The one copied is the one last hovered over.
chart.save.tip: PNG, SVG or PDF — by the extension in the file name. SVG and PDF are vector: they can be enlarged without loss.
chart.detail.tip: What the point under the cursor is. Filled by a click on it — the table with the numbers lives in the main window, and a row highlighted there from another window would be out of sight.
collect.dialog.title: Automatic measurement collection
collect.dialog.intro:
The program creates the containers, mounts them and reads the volumes itself.
An empty volume gives the NTFS metadata — the containers are dynamic, so a terabyte one takes megabytes on disk. A copy-slack measurement writes a generated file set to the volume, and that one needs real space.
collect.dialog.not_found: VeraCrypt was found neither in "C:\Program Files\VeraCrypt" nor in "C:\Program Files (x86)\VeraCrypt". Choose the folder that holds "{format_exe}" and "{mount_exe}".
collect.dialog.install.button.tip:
The folder that holds "{format_exe}" and "{mount_exe}".
Needed if VeraCrypt is not installed in Program Files — a portable build, for example. The choice is remembered.
collect.dialog.version.tip: VeraCrypt's command-line switches have changed over time. For an old version the ones it understands are used; a very old one cannot run the collection.
collect.dialog.workdir.tip:
Folder for the temporary containers — they are deleted right after the measurement.
NTFS measurements need almost no space: the container is dynamic, and only the metadata reaches the disk. A copy-slack measurement writes the whole file set, and that does need space.
collect.dialog.workdir.unavailable: {path} — unavailable or no space at all
collect.dialog.workdir.denied.title: Folder unavailable
collect.dialog.workdir.denied: {path} is not writable — choose another one.
collect.dialog.space.tip:
How much space the hungriest of the chosen steps needs, and how much there is. The requirement is computed by the same metadata model the collection calibrates.
A step that does not fit is skipped — it can be measured later, once space is freed.
collect.dialog.ntfs.tip: Points for the metadata model. Nothing needs to go into the container: the metadata depends only on the volume size.
collect.dialog.everything.tip: Measure every size anew. Makes sense after a Windows update or a change of VeraCrypt version — it is their code that does the formatting.
collect.dialog.self_check: Start with a self-check (1 GiB twice)
collect.dialog.self_check.tip:
Measure one gigabyte two ways: a dynamic container with quick format and a normal one with full format.
If they match, the rest can be measured on dynamic ones. If they differ, this machine cannot do that, and it is better to know at once.
The normal container is the only one in the whole collection that needs a full gigabyte of free space.
collect.dialog.slack: Copy slack — file sets on the volume
collect.dialog.slack.tip: The only part of the model not confirmed by measurements at different file counts. The sets differ precisely in file count: from a single count the slope cannot be computed at all.
collect.dialog.fileset.tip: Container {container} MiB. The calculation promises {predicted} MiB, {safety} MiB of it safety margin; the container is made larger so that the set surely fits, while the prediction is recorded as is — the prediction check rests on it.
collect.dialog.scope.nothing: Nothing to measure: every size is already covered by own measurements.
collect.dialog.scope.summary: Containers to create: {count}. To write: {weight}; the hungriest step needs {peak}.
collect.dialog.scope.short: Steps without enough space: {count} — they will be skipped and can be measured later.
collect.dialog.rights.admin: The program runs with administrator rights — UAC will ask nothing.
collect.dialog.rights.none: No administrator rights: Windows will ask for confirmation for every container. NTFS formatting does not work without them.
collect.dialog.elevate.tip:
Without administrator rights Windows will ask for confirmation for every container, and the collection stops being automatic.
The program will close and open again with the same data folder.
collect.dialog.elevate.confirm.title: Restart as administrator
collect.dialog.elevate.confirm:
The program will close and open again, this time asking for rights. It has nothing unsaved.
Continue?
collect.dialog.elevate.failed.title: Did not work
collect.dialog.elevate.failed: Windows rejected the request for rights. Start the program with "Run as administrator" yourself.
collect.dialog.progress.tip: The share of bytes written, not of steps done. The steps differ too much: an empty terabyte volume is measured in seconds, a four-gigabyte set is written over minutes, and a bar by step count would be off many times over.
collect.dialog.status.tip: Which step is running, which phase it is in, how long this phase has lasted and how much time has passed in all. While a set is written, the files finished and the bytes written are shown.
collect.dialog.log.tip: The course of the collection. The text can be selected and copied — if something went wrong, look here.
collect.dialog.start.confirm.title: Start collection
collect.dialog.start.confirm:
Containers to create and delete: {count}.
About {weight} to write. Continue?
collect.dialog.stop.tip: Stop after finishing what cannot be abandoned. Writing a set is cut off at once, while a container already being created is carried through to the end — otherwise a mounted volume and a file on disk would be left behind.
collect.dialog.close.confirm.title: Collection running
collect.dialog.close.confirm: Stop the collection and close the window? The current container will be finished and deleted, and the window closes after that.
collect.dialog.log.removed: Containers removed from a previous interrupted collection: {count}.
collect.dialog.log.stopping: Stopping as soon as the current step can be abandoned…
collect.dialog.log.negative: ⚠ copy slack came out negative — such a measurement does not go into the copy-slack calibration; its NTFS point stays valid
collect.dialog.log.prediction: prediction: {predicted} MiB promised, {minimum} MiB would have been enough, miss {miss} MiB
collect.dialog.log.done: Done. Measured: {measured}, failed: {failed}, skipped for lack of space: {skipped}.
collect.dialog.log.skipped_later: Skipped steps can be measured later: free some space and open this window again — the missing ones are picked up on their own.
collect.dialog.log.saved: Measurements saved; the tables are already updated.
calibration.intro.title: How to take a point
calibration.intro.text:
By hand: create an empty container of the right size in VeraCrypt with NTFS and quick format, mount it, press "Measure" in its row, then unmount it and delete the file. Nothing needs to go inside — the metadata depends only on the volume size.
"Collect automatically…" does all of this itself, with the same VeraCrypt.
factory.note: Empty containers measured on one machine. Up to 100 GiB, ordinary containers; from 512 MiB, and above 100 GiB, dynamic ones with quick format: on the overlapping sizes the two agreed, because the sparseness of the container file is seen by the host, not by the filesystem inside the volume. The size of the metadata is decided by the formatting code: another Windows build or VeraCrypt version could have chosen a different $LogFile. An own measurement of the same size always supersedes the factory one. Four sizes — 768, 1536, 3072 and 6144 MiB — were taken later by automatic collection and added here: with them every row of the recommended sizes table has a point, and between 512 MiB and 8 GiB the curve no longer rests on sparse samples — that is exactly where it has its staircase.
calibration.collect.tip:
The program creates containers of the missing sizes, measures them and deletes them. By hand that is twenty-two containers and a whole evening.
VeraCrypt must be installed. If it is not in Program Files, we will ask for the folder.
calibration.reset_all.tip: Go back to the factory values at every size. Own measurements stay in the file; the button in a row turns one back on.
calibration.chart.tip:
The NTFS curve from these measurements, the model miss by a leave-one-out check and the slope of each segment — in one window, with a shared axis.
The window is modeless: leave it open alongside and watch the picture change after a new measurement.
calibration.table.tip:
Coverage of the sizes by measurements. Rows go in ascending order and are not sorted.
Hover over a row to see the volume size the measurement is tied to.
calibration.summary.tip: The model calculates uncovered sizes from the neighbouring measurements — that is where it is weakest.
calibration.slack.caption: Copy slack
calibration.slack.explanation:
How much the arrival of files on a volume costs beyond their cluster-rounded size. Taken by the same "Collect automatically…": the program creates a container, writes a generated file set into it and reads the left space.
The file sets differ in file count on purpose — from a single count the per-file slack cannot be told apart from the constant part.
calibration.slack.summary.tip: The miss is counted for each file set separately: the program chose the container for it by itself, and would have missed by itself too.
calibration.slack.table.tip: Own copy-slack measurements. Rows go in the order they were taken and are not sorted.
calibration.col.size.tip: Container init — the number entered in VeraCrypt.
calibration.col.gib.tip: The same size in gibibytes — it makes the row easier to find by eye.
calibration.col.metadata.tip: How much the filesystem keeps for itself on an empty volume: the volume size minus the free space right after formatting. This is the quantity the model predicts.
calibration.col.actions.tip: What can be done with the row: take an own measurement, disable it in favour of the factory one, or bring it back.
calibration.slack_col.fileset.tip: What the file set consisted of. The file sets have different file counts on purpose: from a single count the per-file slack cannot be separated at all.
calibration.slack_col.files.tip: How many files went onto the volume. The per-file slack depends on exactly this number.
calibration.slack_col.alloc.tip: How much the data would take by itself: each file rounded up to a cluster. Everything beyond that is copy slack.
calibration.slack_col.slack.tip: Measured copy slack: the used space on the volume minus the cluster-rounded size of the data. Computed on the fly, not written to the file.
calibration.slack_col.miss.tip: The Container init the calculation promised minus the one that would have just sufficed. Plus is an overestimate, minus — the data would not have fitted.
calibration.slack_col.model_miss.tip: The same miss without the safety margin. Shows whether the models themselves erred: a near underestimate covered by the safety margin would otherwise look healthy.
calibration.slack_col.remove.tip: Delete a measurement. The numbers leave the file entirely — unlike calibration points, there is no point disabling them: there may be no factory value for the same file count at all.
calibration.slack.row.tip: Container {container} MiB, volume capacity {mounted} B, cluster {cluster} B.
calibration.slack.row.predicted: The calculation promised {predicted} MiB, {safety} MiB of it safety margin; {minimum} MiB would have sufficed.
calibration.slack.row.unpredicted: This measurement has no prediction of the calculation — nothing to check against.
calibration.slack.remove.tip: Remove this measurement. It cannot be undone — we will ask for confirmation.
calibration.slack.summary.none: No own copy-slack measurements. Without them the per-file slack remains an assumption, and on a folder of ten thousand files the error carries over into the result in full.
calibration.slack.summary.slope: The slope is computed only with two or more distinct file counts — take one more file set.
calibration.slack.summary.short: The calculation underestimated on {short} of {checked}: {names}. Worst miss {worst} MiB.
calibration.slack.summary.held: The prediction was checked on {checked}: it never underestimated; the smallest overestimate is {worst} MiB, {model} MiB of it the error of the models themselves.
calibration.row.tip:
Container {container} MiB, volume {volume} B — the VeraCrypt headers, {headers} B, are already subtracted.
State: {source}.
calibration.row.take.tip: Measure the empty volume of a {size} MiB container. Nothing needs to go inside.
calibration.row.retake.tip:
Measure the empty volume of a {size} MiB container. Nothing needs to go inside.
The previous measurement at this size will be replaced.
calibration.row.restore.tip: Calculate by the own measurement again — the numbers stayed in the file all along.
calibration.row.reset.tip: Calculate by the factory value. The own measurement stays in the file; this same button brings it back.
calibration.summary: Own measurements: {own}. Factory in use: {factory}. Not covered: {missing}. At the same size an own measurement always takes precedence over the factory one.
measure.title: Measure volume
measure.drive.tip:
The drive letter of the mounted volume. Its capacity, free space, filesystem and cluster size are read from the volume itself.
The list holds every volume in the system, ordinary disks included — choose the container.
measure.details.tip:
Capacity — what the volume reports: the container without the VeraCrypt headers and without the one cluster NTFS keeps for itself.
Free — how much is left on it. On an empty volume, the volume size minus the free space is the NTFS metadata.
The cluster and the filesystem go into the record too.
measure.details.other_profile: ⚠ The measurement goes to the profile {profile}. The calculation so far runs only for {default}, and this measurement takes no part in it.
